h1:
Things to Do in Uttaradit
Nature, Town & Culture
intro: Uttaradit is one of those towns plenty of people just drive past — but it has more worth stopping for than you'd guess. There's the Sirikit Dam, the largest earth-fill dam in Thailand; Phu Soi Dao with its pine meadow and fields of purple Hong Nak flowers; the old town of Lablae with its legend about telling no lies; plus Sukhothai-era temples and the story of Nam Phi steel. We've picked out the spots worth your time, mixing nature, town and culture, whether you're here for a day or staying overnight.

blocks.html: Uttaradit sits on the edge of lower Northern Thailand — just over an hour's drive from Phitsanulok, and close to Sukhothai too. The province stretches from the flat town center up into the mountains to the east, so you can fit several kinds of trip into one visit: walk the old town in the morning, head up to the dam in the afternoon, stop by a temple in the evening. It still doesn't get much tourist traffic, so the mood stays easygoing and you won't be fighting anyone for a photo spot.

blocks.text: For nature lovers — dams, mountains, pine meadows

blocks.html: If you're coming to Uttaradit for nature, the two you can't miss are the Sirikit Dam and Phu Soi Dao. The first is easy — you can drive right up. The second takes some legwork on foot, but it's worth it.

items.name: Sirikit Dam (Tha Pla district)
items.blurb: The largest water-storage earth dam in Thailand, holding back the Nan River. The crest is breezy with a wide reservoir view, and there's Sumalai Park and the Chalermphrakiat Bridge for a walk and photos. Over on the Wang Nam Ton side you can take a raft tour and stay overnight on the water. Free entry.

items.name: Phu Soi Dao National Park
items.blurb: The summit reaches 2,102 metres, among the highest in Thailand. The highlights are the three-needle pine meadow and the fields of purple Hong Nak flowers that bloom in the rainy season around Aug–Sep. You'll hike roughly 6.5 km uphill, so it suits trekkers who've come prepared.

items.name: Lam Nam Nan National Park (Pha Lueat)
items.blurb: Headwater forest above the Sirikit Dam, with ridges folding into one another. There are camping spots and a few short trails — a quiet nature break to fit in on the way to the dam.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Phu Soi Dao only opens seasonally (mainly the rainy season when the Hong Nak flowers bloom), and you need to check the dates and book your slot with the park in advance. Don't just drive all the way up and ask when you get there — you'll waste the trip. The Sirikit Dam, on the other hand, is open year-round and free.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: For the town side — Lablae, markets, old quarter

blocks.html: The charm of Uttaradit town lives in "Lablae" — a small district with a legend that it's a place where you mustn't tell lies. It's easy to wander, between the yellow town gate, the old market, and the orchards all around.

items: Lablae town gate — the bright yellow gate is the landmark at the entrance to the district, with statues from the Lablae legend for a check-in photo.
Si Phanom Mat municipal market (Lablae old market) — an old-style market with pastel wall paintings telling the way of life in earlier times, selling fresh produce, local eats and souvenirs.
Mon Lablae orchards — during fruit season (Jun–Aug), drive through orchards of Lin and Long durian, langsat and longkong, taste them right at the source and buy fresh to take home.

Phraya Phichai monument — in front of the provincial hall in the town center, with a museum inside that tells the history of his battles and a model of an Ayutthaya-era battlefield. It's a key landmark of the town.

blocks.title: Routing
blocks.html: Lablae is only about 8 km from the town center, a 15-minute drive, so it works easily as a morning half-day: walk the market, shoot the town gate, swing by an orchard, then head back into town for lunch.

blocks.text: For culture — old temples and the Nam Phi steel story

blocks.html: Uttaradit has temples dating back to the late Sukhothai period, plus something Thais have known for ages: "Nam Phi steel," a hard steel believed to have been used to forge Phraya Phichai's swords. History buffs and the spiritually inclined will love this zone.

items.name: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At (Lablae district)
items.blurb: An old temple that's a fixture of the town. The highlight is the Phra Thaen Sila At (stone seat) inside its mondop, and there's a local museum displaying paintings, old photographs and antique Thai textiles. The grounds are shady and peaceful.

items.name: Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang
items.blurb: A late-Sukhothai-era temple with the Phra Borommathat Thung Yang chedi enshrining holy relics, plus a principal Buddha image in the Mara-subduing posture in Chiang Saen style. It's an important place of worship for Uttaradit locals.

items.name: Wat Phra Yuen Phutthabat Yukhon
items.blurb: Right near Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang, with a Chiang Saen-style mondop sheltering a pair of Buddha footprints. You can string together your temple visits in the same neighborhood.

items.name: Nam Phi Sword Museum / Nam Phi iron mine (Thong Saen Khan district)
items.blurb: The origin of Nam Phi iron, believed to have forged ancient swords. A large Nam Phi steel sword is on display, with a Pradu-wood scabbard inlaid with mother-of-pearl and silver-wrapped engravings. History fans will come away with plenty of stories to take home.

items.name: Wat Phra Fang (Sawangkhaburi Muninat)
items.blurb: An old temple on the bank of the Nan River, once an important town in the Ayutthaya era, with an old ordination hall and a quiet atmosphere. A good stop for anyone who likes ancient sites that still don't draw many visitors.
items.meta: Temple & historic site · north of town

blocks.title: Group them smartly
blocks.html: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At, Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang and Wat Phra Yuen all sit close together in the Lablae/Thung Yang zone — you can visit them back-to-back in a half-day. The Nam Phi iron site is in a different direction (Thong Saen Khan district), so if you want to go, set aside a separate half-day for it.

blocks.text: How to plan a trip that fits

blocks.html: Uttaradit works for anything from a half-day stop along the way to a full overnight trip. Pick the plan that matches the time you've got.

Drive to Lablae, shoot the town gate, walk Si Phanom Mat market
Try Lablae's famous khao phan phak / mi phan, then carry on

items.activity: Lablae town – old market – orchards (if it's fruit season)
items.note: Start early to catch the market busy

items.activity: Visit Wat Phra Thaen Sila At + Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang
Drive up to the Sirikit Dam, walk the crest and Sumalai Park
Head back into town for dinner
items.note: Avoid driving down the mountain in full dark

Head to the Nam Phi iron mine and sword museum (Thong Saen Khan district)

faq.q: What are the must-do things in Uttaradit?
faq.a: The highlights are the Sirikit Dam (the largest earth dam in Thailand), the town of Lablae with its yellow gate, the Phraya Phichai monument, and Sukhothai-era temples like Wat Phra Thaen Sila At and Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang. If you've got the time and the legs for a hike, Phu Soi Dao when the Hong Nak flowers are blooming is fantastic.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Uttaradit?
faq.a: If you're just grabbing the in-town highlights and Lablae, half a day to one day is enough. But if you want to include the Sirikit Dam, the Nam Phi iron mine and the old temples too, 2 days and 1 night is best so you're not rushing.

faq.q: How should you prepare for Phu Soi Dao?
faq.a: Phu Soi Dao involves a hike of about 6.5 km uphill and only opens seasonally (mainly the rainy season when the Hong Nak flowers bloom, Aug–Sep). You'll need to check the dates and book ahead with the park, and bring hiking shoes, rain gear and a body that's ready for it. It's not a place to drop in on without planning.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit Uttaradit?
faq.a: During fruit season, Jun–Aug, you can eat Lin and Long durian, langsat and longkong fresh from the Lablae orchards. Phu Soi Dao is at its best in the rainy season. And if you'd rather tour the town and temples in comfort without rain, late rainy season into early cool season (Nov–Feb) has just-right weather.

faq.q: What is Lablae, and why is it worth visiting?
faq.a: Lablae is an old district of Uttaradit with a legend that it's a town where you mustn't tell lies. Its draws are the yellow town gate, the old Si Phanom Mat market, and the orchards around it. The mood is quiet and relaxed, good for photos and for tasting local food like khao phan phak and mi phan.
